comment:
* Base class of those Protocol Buffer messages that need to store unknown fields,
 * such as extensions.

variables.name: unknownFieldData
variables.comment:
* A container for fields unknown to the message, including extensions. Extension fields can
     * can be accessed through the {@link #getExtension} and {@link #setExtension} methods.

methods.name: public void writeTo(CodedOutputByteBufferNano output) throws IOException
public final boolean hasExtension(Extension<M, ?> extension)
methods.comment:
* Checks if there is a value stored for the specified extension in this
     * message.

methods.name: public final T getExtension(Extension<M, T> extension)
methods.comment: * Gets the value stored in the specified extension of this message.

methods.name: public final M setExtension(Extension<M, T> extension, T value)
methods.comment: * Sets the value of the specified extension of this message.

methods.name: protected final boolean storeUnknownField(CodedInputByteBufferNano input, int tag) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Stores the binary data of an unknown field. * *

Generated messages will call this for unknown fields if the store_unknown_fields * option is on. * *

Note that the tag might be a end-group tag (rather than the start of an unknown field) in * which case we do not want to add an unknown field entry. * * @param input the input buffer. * @param tag the tag of the field. * @return {@literal true} unless the tag is an end-group tag.
